title: Chapter 94: New Customers
html:
“Xiao Chen, where have you been? Why are you so late for work?” Uncle Xu pulled Chen Ge to stand behind him, afraid that the mob might harm the young man.

“I just came back from the district station; I was helping the police with a murder case.”

“Huh?” Uncle Xu and the surrounding mob stared at him. People usually blamed traffic or an upset stomach for arriving late. A murder investigation was a new one.

“A murder case?” Uncle Xu stared at Chen Ge, the urgent situation momentarily forgotten.

“Yes, but this case is different from the murders at the apartment. It probably won’t make the news.”

There was an earlier murder?The raging mob’s aggression suddenly dwindled.

“All right, leave this to me.” Chen Ge faced the crowd. “You’re looking for me?”

That single question extinguished what little momentum the mob had left. The crowd exchanged glances, then pushed their shortest member, a middle-aged man, forward to face him.

“We represent Qin Guang’s studio. Last night, you resorted to unethical tactics, hiring paid trolls to spread rumors and damage Qin Guang’s reputation.”

“I used unethical tactics? You certainly know how to invent a story. You know perfectly well who the real plagiarist is.” Chen Ge cut him off. “If that’s all, please leave. You’re interfering with my business.”

“Qin Guang merely chose the same location for his livestream. The fact that you filmed there first does not make his work plagiarism.” The middle-aged man stood his ground.

“Compare the two streams. Qin Guang even copied the analysis I gave while trapped in the bedroom. If that isn’t plagiarism, what is?”

“At most, he borrowed your opening. Everything afterward was his own creative work. You can’t call that plagiarism. At worst, it was an homage.”

Chen Ge had never encountered such shamelessness. Reasoning with them was clearly pointless, so he walked past, opened the gate, and prepared for business.

“You’re new, so we understand your ambition, but this industry isn’t so simple.” The man pulled a document from his bag. At first, Chen Ge mistook it for a lawyer’s letter, but that gave his opponent too much credit.

“You don’t work in this industry, so you don’t understand how it operates. Money and exposure create successful hosts. You may be popular today, but the platform will never abandon Qin Guang for a newcomer. He’s one of their flagship hosts; his success benefits them too.” The man waved the document. “Stop attacking him and issue a public apology, and we’ll compensate you. Keep harassing him and his associates to boost your own profile, and we’ll have the platform ban you from every channel.”

“Don’t shift the blame onto the viewers. They saw blatant bullying and chose to support me.” The threat meant nothing to Chen Ge. The platform had never helped him, and even he did not quite understand how he had gained his current popularity.

“Rash decisions help no one. Why not think it over?” The man’s attitude had softened considerably. Six of them had come looking for trouble, but Chen Ge’s opening remark had derailed their plan. It was understandable. Anyone would become cautious upon learning that the man before them had been involved in not one but two murder cases.

“There’s nothing to consider. I already know what makes my livestreams and videos unique. Even if I’m forced off this platform, I’ll rebuild my audience elsewhere.” Chen Ge shooed Qin Guang’s people aside and told Xu Wan to prepare for business.

After running around all night, Chen Ge was exhausted. He settled into the booth to sell tickets. Once the first few groups emerged from the Haunted House, Qin Guang’s people returned.

“You people don’t give up! If you’re not here for the Haunted House, move aside. You’re blocking actual customers!” Even a saint would lose patience under such harassment, and Chen Ge had already been polite enough.

“Who said we aren’t customers? We’d like to experience the so-called scariest Haunted House in Jiujiang.” Two young men from the studio stepped forward, backpacks slung over their shoulders.

“You also want to visit the Haunted House?” Naturally, Chen Ge suspected that these people were up to no good.

“If you’re afraid we’ll expose your false advertising, fine. We won’t go in.” One of the young men was heavily muscled and wore a tank top clearly chosen to display the results of his training.

The man’s challenge pricked at Chen Ge. “Let me remind you—the last person who said that came out on his back.”

“You’ve only made me more interested.” Beside the muscular man stood a meek-looking man in glasses. “I’ve watched horror movies since childhood. Before Brother Qin recruited me, I worked on a horror film crew. Unfortunately, most sets looked too fake to be frightening.”

“I do love customers who are always searching for a greater scare.” Chen Ge drew back the curtain. “Come in, then. Just remember to sign the waiver.”

He would hardly turn away willing test subjects. Even his smile grew noticeably more sincere.

At the smile on Chen Ge’s face, Uncle Xu shuddered. He remembered the forensic students from Jiujiang Medical University sprawled helplessly across the floor.

Uncle Xu coughed and pulled him to the side. “Xiao Chen, don’t go overboard. Remember, they are still park visitors.”

Before Chen Ge could answer, the bespectacled man scoffed, convinced he had seen through their act. “Well, well. Impressive performance. Does the show begin before we even enter?

“I read the reviews before coming. Plenty of people said the owner knew some psychology. It seems they weren’t lying.”

Uncle Xu stared at the young man, speechless. I’m trying to help you. If you weren’t likely to die in there, I wouldn’t care what happened!

“Uncle Xu, I know the limits. Don’t worry.” Chen Ge personally led the two men inside and watched them sign the waivers.

The larger, muscular man was called Zhu Jianing, and the bespectacled man was Fei Youliang.
